answer: A prism gauge signs each tide crest so the port can pay agents that relay it on time. Each key may buy one permit per crest. On purchase the ledger burns $0.02 times the global permit index, starting at 1 each crest, and redeems each permit once with a signed reading. An honest first relay spends $0.02. At 1,000 aliases the fees total at least $10,010 for at most $1,000 in bounties. A bot cannot forge a receipt because validators read burns on-chain and bind each to its key and crest. Bots can still win cheap early permits, and prices restart at the next crest.
